text:
deploy-bot: Rolling out v2026.03.19-rc1 to eu-west-1 (canary 5%). Post-deploy smoke suite starting: warmup-heartbeat, kv-prefill, tokenizer-sanity. Initial health: warmup-heartbeat p95 = 850ms (baseline 420ms), kv-prefill 429s = 0.6% (threshold 0.5%).

sara: noticed the warmup p95 double. Is this correlated with the new pooling change landed in runtime PR#782?

devon: yes, PR#782 changes the allocator backoff and adds a short prefill concurrency bump. we expected better cold-starts, not worse.

synth-watchdog: failing probes: 8/120 (6.7%) across warmup-heartbeat and kv-prefill. Hosts: eu-w1-prefill-03, eu-w1-prefill-04, eu-w1-gpu-02. Error excerpts: "prefill throttle" and "tokenizer init slow: 1.1s".

infra-oncall: pulling host metrics. eu-w1-prefill-03 CPU 92% for prefill-worker; queue depth x9. Memory OK. Autoscaler hasn't taken extra pods.

sara: we have a 1-hour change window for this release. decision: do we 1) pause canary and pin hosts to previous runtime, 2) reduce canary to 1% and route prefills to stable path, or 3) full rollback of the rollout? We should also update the change window notes.

devon: prefer option 2: reduce canary and fallback prefill routing. That keeps release moving while we quick-fix autoscaler config. Option 1 is more targeted but requires host pinning which is slower to enact across pool.

synth-watchdog: guideline: if probe failures > 1% persist after mitigation, escalate to rollback. Current is 0.6% so option 2 safe.

autopilot-bot: suggested command: `deploy-bot modify-rollout --model rwd-t5-pool --canary 1 --route-prefill stable --note "temp fallback during autoscaler tuning"`

sara: execute that command and add a note to release notes under "Canary adjustments". Also log the change in the change-window: `Change window: 60m; action: mitigated by prefill fallback and canary reduction.`

deploy-bot: Executing: `deploy-bot modify-rollout --model rwd-t5-pool --canary 1 --route-prefill stable` — completed in 14s. Estimated time for prefills to normalize: 2m.

synth-watchdog: scheduled recheck in 120s. Will monitor kv-prefill 429 rate and warmup-heartbeat p95.

(2m later)
synth-watchdog: recheck: kv-prefill 429s down to 0.08%, warmup-heartbeat p95 reduced to 470ms (1.12x baseline). No additional host failures.

sara: good. Update release notes: "Canary: temporarily reduced to 1% and prefills routed to stable runtime due to prefill worker queueing observed in early canary. Investigation of PR#782 allocator change ongoing; target follow-up in post-release retro."

devon: I'll revert the allocator backoff flag in a dev build and run a focused soak with prefill rates x3 to reproduce. If repro, we'll open RW-1445 for the runtime fix.

infra-oncall: setting ephemeral alert: `prefill_429 > 0.5% for 10m` -> pager. Monitoring for 60m.

sara: because we're inside the change window, I'll mark this as a 'mitigated-canary' event in the release tracker and add to the release notes seed. No full rollback required.

autopilot-bot: reminder: To resume original rollout after fixes use `deploy-bot resume-rollout --model rwd-t5-pool --canary 5`

synth-watchdog: final status (45m later): probes stable, no regressions detected. closing thread; please attach any repro logs to RW-1445 if found.

sara: thanks all. I'll file the short incident summary and add a line in the release changelog and the post-deploy checklist: "Include 10m prefill soak at current canary percent to catch autoscaler regressions." :white_check_mark:

devon: adding logs to RW-1445 and scheduling a short retro with runtime and perf teams.
